entries.reason: the time the buffer's work started, which this port takes from the first command the buffer encodes, since the port runs each command as it is encoded
entries.effect: 0 until the buffer has completed, then the start of its work on the media clock (CACurrentMediaTime); the same span as kernelStartTime, because the port has one processor
entries.source: SDK 16.4, Metal; the relations (zero before completion, positive and ordered after) measured on the host in tests/backports/device/commandbuffer-probe/host-expectations.txt; the values are not comparable across clocks

entries.reason: the time the buffer's work ended, which this port takes at the end of its commit, when the work of every encoder of the buffer has run
entries.effect: 0 until the buffer has completed, then the end of its commit on the media clock, not before GPUStartTime
entries.source: SDK 16.4, Metal; the relations measured on the host in tests/backports/device/commandbuffer-probe/host-expectations.txt

entries.reason: the kernel's span, which on this port is the GPU's span: the one processor runs the kernels and the rest of the buffer's work in the same span
entries.effect: 0 until completion, then the same value as GPUStartTime; Metal reports its kernel span inside its GPU span, and the port's two spans are equal, a difference the facts file names
entries.source: SDK 16.4, Metal; the relations measured on the host in tests/backports/device/commandbuffer-probe/host-expectations.txt

entries.reason: the kernel's end, which on this port is the GPU's end, for the same reason as kernelStartTime
entries.effect: 0 until completion, then the same value as GPUEndTime
entries.source: SDK 16.4, Metal; the relations measured on the host in tests/backports/device/commandbuffer-probe/host-expectations.txt
